# journal

```go
import "github.com/danmestas/dagnats/journal"
```

journal/floor.go The protected floor: the lowest AGENT\_JOURNAL sequence that a later Open of a live step still reads. An archiver that purges the journal below what it has archived must also stay below this floor, because agent steps read their journal on every delivery \(Open replays the iteration's model and tool calls\), and those reads hold no consumer ack floor an archiver could see.

What Open reads \(rebuild\): the state of the newest commit of an earlier iteration, and every record of the iteration it claims. So a step on iteration N needs iteration N\-1's last commit and N's records, and nothing older; a parked chat run does not pin the journal from its first turn. A step with no earlier commit, or whose records carry no iteration, is protected from its first record. A fork is protected from its first record too, and so is every parent journal of its chain, which Open reads up to the fork point.

Placements of earlier iterations \(input.placed\) fall below the floor. Open keeps them to refuse placing a request twice, but a placement is settled done in the submissions bucket when its iteration commits, and a done submission is never placed again.

journal/fork.go Forks \(\#810\). A forked step's journal starts with one fork record naming a parent journal and a sequence in it. Open then treats the parent's records up to and including that sequence as this step's history: the parent's committed state before the forked iteration is the state, and the forked iteration's records up to the point are replayed by position as the forked step's iteration 0, so model responses and tool results recorded before the point are reused and execution diverges after it. The parent journal is only read.

The parent's records must still be in AGENT\_JOURNAL: a fork cannot read records archived out of the stream.

journal/inputs.go Placement records \(ADR\-027\). An input moves from the submissions bucket into the conversation by one input.placed record; the record is the truth about placement, so a journal knows every request\_id placed in any iteration and a successor never places one twice.

Package journal is the agent journal of ADR\-026: one append\-only JetStream subject per step, journal.\{run\}.\{step\}, where an agent step's SDK records what it did so a successor can take over without repeating a turn. Every append is fenced on the journal tail its writer last saw, so a worker that lost the tail \(stalled past its AckWait, superseded by a redelivery\) cannot write, and is told so.

A Journal is one claim on one dispatch of a step. Open reads the tail from the stream leader, stops without writing when the step has moved to a later iteration, rebuilds what this iteration needs from the records so far, and appends a claim record. Append and Commit then carry Nats\-Expected\-Last\-Subject\-Sequence and a stable Nats\-Msg\-Id. A rejected append is not fencing by itself: the writer re\-reads the tail and only a record from another claim of the same or a later iteration fences it.

## Variables

<a name="ErrArchive"></a>

```go
var (
    // ErrArchive: a journal read needed records below the stream's
    // FirstSeq and the archive could not supply all of them (no
    // archive, not archived, unknown epoch, a gap, busy, timeout).
    ErrArchive = errors.New("journal: records purged from JetStream could not be read " +
        "from the archive")
    // ErrDiscontinuous: a record names a predecessor the read does not
    // hold, or the records are out of order. Replay cannot be trusted.
    ErrDiscontinuous = errors.New("journal: record chain is broken")
)
```

<a name="ErrForkNoJournal"></a>Fork errors.

```go
var (
    // ErrForkNoJournal: the parent step has no journal, so it is not
    // an agent step there is anything to fork from.
    ErrForkNoJournal = errors.New("journal: the parent step has no journal")
    // ErrForkPoint: the sequence is not a record of the parent step's
    // journal that a fork may start from (a commit or fork record is
    // not one), or the record is no longer in the stream.
    ErrForkPoint = errors.New("journal: the sequence is not a fork point in the parent journal")
    // ErrForkExists: the forked step's journal already holds records.
    ErrForkExists = errors.New("journal: the forked step's journal is not empty")
)
```

<a name="ErrStale"></a>Sentinel errors a handler is expected to check.

```go
var (
    // ErrStale: the journal tail belongs to a later iteration, so this
    // task is a late redelivery. Nothing was written; the task is done.
    ErrStale = errors.New("journal: task is stale, a later iteration holds the step")
    // ErrFenced: a record from another claim follows this writer's.
    // Nothing more may be written or published for this task.
    ErrFenced = errors.New("journal: fenced by another claim")
    // ErrCommitted: this attempt already committed the iteration.
    // Open found the commit; the caller republishes its event.
    ErrCommitted = errors.New("journal: iteration already committed by this attempt")
    // ErrRestartLimit: the crash-loop guard failed the step (ADR-028).
    // The worker has published step.failed; the handler must return.
    ErrRestartLimit = errors.New("journal: restart limit reached, the step has been failed")
    // ErrNotProvisioned: the stream is missing.
    ErrNotProvisioned = errors.New(
        "journal: AGENT_JOURNAL stream not provisioned" +
            " — ensure natsutil.SetupAll() has been called" +
            " or start the server with 'dagnats serve'",
    )
)
```

<a name="ErrFloorOverBudget"></a>ErrFloorOverBudget: the live journals hold more runs, subjects or records than one floor pass reads. No floor is computed; a caller that publishes it leaves the published one to go stale.

```go
var ErrFloorOverBudget = errors.New("journal: protected floor pass is over its budget")
```

<a name="ErrReplayMismatch"></a>ErrReplayMismatch: the call at this position was recorded with another name or input. The handler is not replaying the sequence of calls it recorded; nothing is reused or written.

```go
var ErrReplayMismatch = errors.New("journal: tool call does not match the recorded call")
```

<a name="ArchivedBefore"></a>
## func [ArchivedBefore](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/archive.go#L108-L111>)

```go
func ArchivedBefore(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream, subject string, from uint64, live *jetstream.RawStreamMsg, limit int) ([]dagnatsext.ArchivedMessage, error)
```

ArchivedBefore returns the archived messages of subject from sequence from up to the live record live, which JetStream still holds: nothing when live's predecessor is below from, so the read needs no archive. limit bounds the messages \(0: recordsMax\). Without a limit cutting it short the last one must be live's predecessor. For the engine relay, which answers a program's journal reads; Read and Open use it inside.

<a name="ArchivedFrom"></a>

```go
func ArchivedFrom(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream, subject string, from uint64, limit int) (msgs []dagnatsext.ArchivedMessage, purged bool, err error)
```

ArchivedFrom reads up to limit archived messages of subject from sequence from, for a read that found nothing in JetStream at or after from. purged is false, and nothing is asked, when the stream was never purged at or after from.

<a name="CheckContinuity"></a>
## func [CheckContinuity](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/archive.go#L76>)

```go
func CheckContinuity(records []Record, from uint64) error
```

CheckContinuity verifies that records, read from sequence from, form an unbroken chain on their subject: each record's predecessor is the record before it, and the first one's is below from. A record that carries no predecessor header is not checked against its neighbour.

<a name="MsgID"></a>
## func [MsgID](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/journal.go#L269>)

```go
func MsgID(task Task, index int) string
```

MsgID is the stable dedup key of a record: \{run\}.\{step\}.\{attempt\}.\{iteration\}.\{stream\_seq\}.\{delivered\}.\{index\}. The delivery count keeps a redelivery's records distinct from the stalled delivery's inside the dedup window; the stream sequence does the same for a resend, which restarts the count. Without them the successor's claim would be answered with the old claim's sequence.

<a name="OpenNeedsNothingBefore"></a>
## func [OpenNeedsNothingBefore](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/archive.go#L284>)

```go
func OpenNeedsNothingBefore(hdr nats.Header, iteration int) bool
```

OpenNeedsNothingBefore reports whether a record with these headers is the commit of an iteration before iteration. Open of that iteration starts from the newest such commit and reads nothing older \(\#980's protected floor sits at it\), so a journal purged below it opens without the archive. The engine relay applies the same rule.

<a name="ProtectedFloor"></a>
## func [ProtectedFloor](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/floor.go#L62-L65>)

```go
func ProtectedFloor(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream, listRuns func(context.Context) ([]string, error)) (uint64, error)
```

ProtectedFloor returns the lowest AGENT\_JOURNAL sequence a later Open of a step of a live run still reads: the minimum over every journal of the runs listRuns names. With no such journal it is the stream's LastSeq\+1, protecting nothing. listRuns is called after the stream's LastSeq is read, so a run that goes live after the list writes only above the returned floor.

<a name="Journal"></a>
## type [Journal](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/journal.go#L209-L261>)

Journal is one claim on one dispatch of a step. A handle belongs to one goroutine: replay matches tool and model calls by position, so calls issued from several goroutines would replay in another order. A handler running a model's parallel tool calls issues them through the journal one at a time. Concurrent use panics; a tool function may call back into the journal from the goroutine that owns it.

```go
type Journal struct {
    // contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

<a name="Open"></a>
### func [Open](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/journal.go#L288-L291>)

```go
func Open(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream, pub *natsutil.TracingPublisher, task Task) (*Journal, error)
```

Open claims task's dispatch. It returns ErrStale when the tail belongs to a later iteration \(nothing written\), ErrFenced when a rival claim for the same iteration won, and a journal whose Committed reports this attempt's own commit when the previous holder crashed between committing and publishing \(no claim is appended then\).

<a name="Journal.Model"></a>
### func \(\*Journal\) [Model](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/replay.go#L466>)

```go
func (j *Journal) Model(ctx context.Context, fn ModelFunc) ([]byte, error)
```

Model requests one model response durably: the response a previous holder of this attempt recorded for the call at this position is returned without calling fn; otherwise fn runs and its response is appended as model.response. A request that fails records nothing and leaves the position free, and a new attempt of the iteration requests afresh. Streaming tokens are not the journal's business: PutStream is a non\-durable preview, and a crash mid\-stream re\-sends the request on the next delivery. Model must be called from the goroutine that owns the handle.

<a name="Journal.Restarts"></a>
### func \(\*Journal\) [Restarts](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/journal.go#L467>)

```go
func (j *Journal) Restarts() int
```

Restarts returns how many claims on this iteration sat at the tail before this claim with nothing between them: deliveries that claimed and then made no progress. A pause, an entry, a tool or model record, or a commit resets the count; a claim after a commit \(a retry\) starts from 0. Feeds the worker's restart limit \(ADR\-028\).

<a name="Journal.Tool"></a>
### func \(\*Journal\) [Tool](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/replay.go#L115-L117>)

```go
func (j *Journal) Tool(ctx context.Context, call ToolCall, replay Replay, fn ToolFunc) (ToolResult, error)
```

Tool runs one tool call durably: it appends the call's intent with its replay declaration, runs fn, and appends the result. Calls are matched by position within the iteration, and a recorded call at the position must be the same call \(name and input\), else ErrReplayMismatch. On a claim that recovers an attempt a previous holder started: a recorded result is returned without running fn; an intent without a result is rerun only when the recorded and the current declaration both say Safe, and otherwise answered with an interrupted result carrying the partial output and the call's key, which the model then sees. On a new attempt of the iteration \(after a commit, or a higher attempt from iteration 1\) only unsafe intents are honoured, matched by content rather than position: the first prior unsafe intent with the same name and input not yet honoured in this attempt answers the call under its own key, with its recorded result or as interrupted; safe calls run afresh. A call that takes a position in a new attempt skips the positions prior unsafe intents hold, so it never shares their keys.

The guarantee is that the SDK starts an unsafe call at most once per position. A holder stalled between its intent and the tool's effect may still complete that effect after a successor recorded the call as interrupted; the key is what an external system deduplicates on. The returned error is the journal's \(ErrFenced, ErrCommitted, transport\), never the tool's own, which is in the result. Tool must be called from the goroutine that owns the handle; a model's parallel tool calls are issued one at a time.

<a name="ArchivedPrefix"></a>
### func [ArchivedPrefix](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/archive.go#L394-L397>)

```go
func ArchivedPrefix(ctx context.Context, js jetstream.JetStream, runID, stepID string, from uint64, limit int, history bool) ([]Record, error)
```

ArchivedPrefix returns the step's records from sequence from that are only in the archive: empty when the first record at or after from is still in JetStream with no purged predecessor at or after from, or when JetStream holds nothing there. At most limit records \(0: recordsMax\). The client journal read \(GET .../journal\) serves them before its JetStream page. history says the step may have had records \(a later iteration or a retry\): only then is a step JetStream holds nothing of at or after from read from the archive.

Report is the result of Check for one run.

```go

    RunID string       `json:"run_id"`
    Steps []StepReport `json:"steps"`
```

<a name="Check"></a>
### func [Check](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/check.go#L63>)

```go
func Check(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, runID string) (Report, error)
```

Check audits a run's journals against its history and snapshot: each iteration has exactly one commit from the attempt the engine accepted \(1\); no record follows the claim that fenced its writer \(2\); every tool.intent has one tool.result \(4\); every placed input appears once \(5\); the engine's iteration count equals the accepted continue commits \(6\). Invariant 3 needs a side\-effect counter outside the journal and is reported as skipped, as is 5 while the submissions bucket does not exist.


OK reports whether no step has a violation.

<a name="Task"></a>
## type [Task](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/journal.go#L111-L131>)

Task identifies one dispatch of a step: the identity every record carries and every lifecycle event names \(ADR\-025\).

```go
type Task struct {
    RunID         string
    StepID        string
    Iteration     int
    Attempt       int
    DispatchNonce string
    // Delivered is the delivery count of the task message. It is part
    // of the claim identity: the engine stamps the attempt on every
    // dispatch, so a stalled worker and the AckWait redelivery that
    // replaces it share run, step, iteration, attempt and nonce, and
    // only the delivery count tells their claims apart. It also orders
    // the deliveries of one message (a newer one fences an older one
    // opening after it) and feeds the crash-loop guard (#807).
    Delivered int
    // StreamSeq is the task message's sequence in the task stream.
    // Redeliveries share it; a dispatch resend is a fresh message with
    // a new one and delivery count 1 again, so only it tells a resend's
    // claim from the original's while that is still in flight. Zero
    // when unknown.
    StreamSeq uint64
}
```

<a name="ToolCall"></a>
## type [ToolCall](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/replay.go#L45-L50>)

ToolCall is one tool invocation. The handler sets Name and Input; Tool fills Call \(the call's position in the iteration, counting from 0\) and Key, the idempotency key \{run\}.\{step\}.\{iteration\}.\{call\}, which is the same on every delivery of an attempt so the tool can hand it to an external system that deduplicates. A new attempt keeps a prior unsafe call's key when it honours the call; a fresh call's position, and so its key, can differ between attempts.

```go
type ToolCall struct {
    Name  string          `json:"name"`
    Input json.RawMessage `json:"input,omitempty"`
    Call  int             `json:"call"`
    Key   string          `json:"key"`
}
```

<a name="ToolFunc"></a>
## type [ToolFunc](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/replay.go#L56>)

ToolFunc runs the tool. The output it returns must be a JSON value, because it is recorded as is: encode plain text with json.Marshal. The error it returns is the tool's own failure, recorded in the result for the model to see; it is not a reason to stop the step.

```go
type ToolFunc func(ctx context.Context, call ToolCall) ([]byte, error)
```

<a name="ToolResult"></a>
## type [ToolResult](<https://github.com/danmestas/dagnats/blob/main/journal/replay.go#L70-L77>)

ToolResult is the body of a tool.result record. Key is the call's idempotency key. Interrupted marks a call a previous holder started and never finished, which was not rerun; Partial then holds, as a JSON array, the entry records that holder appended while the tool ran.

```go
type ToolResult struct {
    Call        int             `json:"call"`
    Key         string          `json:"key"`
    Output      json.RawMessage `json:"output,omitempty"`
    Error       string          `json:"error,omitempty"`
    Interrupted bool            `json:"interrupted,omitempty"`
    Partial     json.RawMessage `json:"partial,omitempty"`
}
```
